boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten nearby Brooklyn corridors, each paired with a named destination documented by a primary public, cultural, university, or venue source.

cards.title: Pratt Institute Brooklyn Campus
cards.subtitle: Willoughby Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Walk the Willoughby Avenue edge and use Pratt’s official campus map to orient yourself before exploring the public-facing streets nearby.
cards.short_summary: A documented arts-and-design campus address on Willoughby Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Pratt Institute lists its Brooklyn Campus at 200 Willoughby Avenue, Brooklyn, NY 11205.
cards.access_notes: Pratt directs visitors to plan ahead for campus tours; consult its visitor page for current details.

cards.title: Brooklyn Navy Yard Building 77
cards.subtitle: Flushing Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use the Flushing Avenue approach to locate Building 77, then consult the Yard’s visitor information for public offerings and entry guidance.
cards.short_summary: Building 77 is a public-facing Brooklyn Navy Yard destination on Flushing Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The Brooklyn Navy Yard identifies Building 77 at 141 Flushing Avenue and describes Building 77 and Building 92 as visitor destinations.
cards.access_notes: Check the Yard’s current gate-access information before entering; access conditions can change.

cards.title: Commodore Barry Park
cards.subtitle: Park Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Enter from the Park Avenue side and use the city’s facilities list to choose an activity that fits your visit, such as courts or open space.
cards.short_summary: A city park at the Park Avenue and Navy Street area.
cards.evidence_claim: NYC Parks places Commodore Barry Park between Nassau Street and Park Avenue, from Navy Street to North Elliott Place, and lists athletic and recreation facilities.
cards.access_notes: Use the NYC Parks page for current facility information and directions.

cards.title: Fort Greene Park
cards.subtitle: Myrtle Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Approach from Myrtle Avenue and follow the park paths toward the monument, courts, or lawns; check NYC Parks for current programming first.
cards.short_summary: A 30-acre public park bordered in part by Myrtle Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: NYC Parks identifies Fort Greene Park at Myrtle and DeKalb Avenues between Washington Park and St. Edward’s Street and lists it as 30.17 acres.
cards.source_title: Fort Greene Park Capital Projects — NYC Parks
cards.access_notes: Construction and event activity may affect particular entrances or paths; review the NYC Parks page before going.

cards.title: Brooklyn Academy of Music
cards.subtitle: Lafayette Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use Lafayette Avenue to find BAM’s Peter Jay Sharp Building and consult its calendar or box office information before selecting a program.
cards.short_summary: A performing-arts institution located at 30 Lafayette Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: BAM lists its address as 30 Lafayette Avenue, Brooklyn, NY 11217.
cards.access_notes: Programs and tickets vary; check BAM’s current schedule and visitor information.

cards.title: BRIC House
cards.subtitle: Fulton Street corridor
cards.notes: Stop at 647 Fulton Street to see BRIC’s cultural center, then check its gallery, media-center, and event details for the day you visit.
cards.short_summary: A multidisciplinary arts and media complex on Fulton Street.
cards.evidence_claim: BRIC states that BRIC House is at 647 Fulton Street and includes a gallery, media center, performance spaces, and community programming.
cards.access_notes: BRIC publishes current building and gallery hours on its official visitor information.

cards.title: Classon Playground
cards.subtitle: Classon Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use the Lafayette and Classon intersection as your reference point, and bring simple court gear if you plan to use the listed handball courts.
cards.short_summary: A city playground identified at Lafayette and Classon Avenues.
cards.evidence_claim: NYC Parks lists Classon Playground at Lafayette and Classon Avenues and identifies handball courts there.
cards.access_notes: Check NYC Parks for facility conditions and any scheduled maintenance.

cards.title: Washington Hall Park
cards.subtitle: Washington Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Find the park at Washington Avenue and Hall Street, then use its courts or playground area according to posted rules and current conditions.
cards.short_summary: A named city park at the Washington Avenue and Hall Street intersection.
cards.evidence_claim: NYC Parks lists Washington Hall Park at Washington Avenue and Hall Street and identifies four handball courts at the site.
cards.access_notes: Facilities are managed by NYC Parks; review posted rules when you arrive.

cards.title: Steuben Playground
cards.subtitle: Steuben Street corridor
cards.notes: Use Steuben Street at Flushing Avenue as the landmark, and bring a ball only if you plan to use the playground’s listed handball courts.
cards.short_summary: A city recreation stop at the Steuben Street and Flushing Avenue junction.
cards.evidence_claim: NYC Parks lists Steuben Playground at Flushing Avenue and Steuben Street and identifies two handball courts.
cards.access_notes: Check NYC Parks for current facility information before planning organized play.

cards.title: Barclays Center
cards.subtitle: Atlantic Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use the Atlantic Avenue entrance area to locate the arena and consult its official event calendar, transit guidance, and venue policies before attending.
cards.short_summary: A major event venue at the Atlantic Avenue–Barclays Center transit hub.
cards.evidence_claim: Barclays Center’s official site identifies the venue at 620 Atlantic Avenue in Brooklyn and provides event and visitor information.
cards.access_notes: Admission and age policies depend on the event; verify the specific event’s requirements before purchasing.
